title: 90-day horizon ops brief and staff commitment catalog
body:
Purpose:
This is a working brief to align leadership and team owners on a 90-day horizon (Q4 preview -> next quarter start) that stitches OKR candidates, an exec update narrative, and a lightweight all-team run-of-show. Goal: surface tradeoffs, firm up staffing asks, and leave the meeting with a prioritized commitment catalog that teams can convert into tickets.

Scope and assumptions:
- Timebox: 90 days from 2025-11-01 to 2026-01-30 (covers ramp into next FY quarter).
- Focus pillars: Reliability & SLAs, Unit-cost reduction (Optimize), Private deployments & compliance, Developer experience (onboarding, docs).
- Healthy constraint: Keep two cross-functional rollouts at most (to avoid over-commitment during holiday ramp).

Top-level narrative for exec update (draft):
- Headline: "Stabilize the base, accelerate predictable economics"
- Problem: recent spikes in tail latency and increased per-token cost for medium-length sequences are impacting pilot customers.
- Thesis: Prioritize three mech-level interventions (KV-cache improvements, batching tuning, Dedicated quantization pilot) that deliver both reduced P95 latency and measurable token-cost savings.
- Ask: Exec sign-off for a short reserve pool (Dedicated burst capacity) pilot and 4 FTEs reallocated (2 infra SRE, 1 applied-ML, 1 product PM) for 10 weeks.
- KPIs to commit to publicly in the exec update: P95 latency delta, tokens/unit cost improvement, number of successful private deployments (VPC) completed.

Candidate OKRs (drafts — objective, top 2 key results):
- Objective A: Reduce production tail latency and improve SLA confidence
  - KR1: Decrease P95 generation latency for serving-runtime by 25% on 8k token profiles
  - KR2: Ship tracing hooks and automated alerting for three root causes (cache misses, stall batching, memory pressure) with <5min MTTD on incidents

- Objective B: Lower per-token inference cost for top 10 customers
  - KR1: Deliver batching + quantization recommendations that lower average tokens/unit cost by 18% for heavy-medium workloads
  - KR2: Complete Dedicated burst pilot and evaluate cost delta vs hosted for two representative workloads (report ROI)

- Objective C: Increase enterprise adoption readiness for Private deployments
  - KR1: Onboard 3 regulated customers into Private with completed security review and baseline perf tests
  - KR2: Deliver KMS/HSM integration blueprint and two-step runbook for audit evidence collection

- Objective D: Developer velocity and onboarding
  - KR1: Reduce time-to-first-successful-call via Redwood Console by 40% for new signups (measured by first-week active SDK usage)
  - KR2: Publish 5 end-to-end templates (embeddings, reranking, streaming chat, eval harness, canary rule) with sample prompts and eval suites

Prioritization notes and rationale:
- We prefer first-order engineering work with durable impact (caching + batching) over speculative large-model experiments in this window.
- Private deployment push is revenue-sensitive; needs legal + security runway — we propose a gated cadence: triage -> security hardening -> pilot customer onboarding.
- Developer experience wins have high leverage on PLG funnel; allocate a small squad to ship the top 2 quick wins.

Staff commitment catalog (high-level owners and approx effort estimates):
- infra-sre: KV cache algorithm increment + tracing hooks — owner: Omar Ruiz — est 6w (2x SREs part-time)
- serving-runtime: batching tuning + kernel selection telemetry — owner: Daniel Park — est 8w (2 engs full-time)
- applied-ml: quantization pilot + perf profile for Dedicated — owner: Asha Kapoor — est 6w (1 engineer full-time, 1 researcher part-time)
- product/console: onboarding templates + canary workflows — owner: Grace Liu — est 4w (1 PM + 1 DX eng)
- security/legal: Private pilot review and runbook — owner: Lina Morales (legal) — est 3w (coord effort)

Run-of-show for company sync / all-team (45–60min):
1) 5m — Opening by CEO (northstar + 90-day ask)
2) 8m — Headline metrics and problem statement (VP Eng)
3) 10m — Short arc: three interventions (SRE, Serving, Private) with owners and expected impact
4) 7m — Ask to staff: where we need temporary reassignments and hiring priorities
5) 10m — Breakouts / quick triage: product, infra, applied-ml (pre-assigned leads)
6) 5–10m — Close + concrete next steps and where to find the commitment ticket board

Communications checklist (pre-all-hands):
- Draft exec email and FAQ for staff (FAQ must include: why reassignments, what happens to postponed projects, who keeps product support).
- Commitment board (template): GitHub project with columns: Proposed -> Committed -> In-flight -> Done; link in the doc and show at all-hands.
- Visuals: one slide showing the 90-day gantt, one slide showing the staff commitment catalog (owner + #weeks), one slide of KPI dashboard.

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: Holiday coverage + hiring freeze might constrain headcount reallocation; contingency: narrow scope to single quantization pilot + KV-cache improvement.
- Question: Do we make the Dedicated burst pool a chargeable pilot or absorptive cost for Q4? (finance input needed)
- Risk: Private pilot security sign-off timelines are uncertain; include legal at triage to avoid late blockers.

Decisions needed before publish (timeline):
- By 2025-11-10: Exec confirmation on FTE reassignments and Dedicated pilot budget (owner: CFO + CEO)
- By 2025-11-15: Finalized OKR wording and public KPI definitions (owner: Head of Product + Eng)
- By 2025-11-20: All-hands deck and email ready (owner: Comms + Head of People)

Next steps (owner + immediate action):
- Maya Chen: consolidate feedback from infra/product leads (due 2025-11-07)
- Omar Ruiz: draft SRE workplan & gating criteria (due 2025-11-09)
- Asha Kapoor: initial quant pilot plan + evaluation matrix (due 2025-11-09)
- Grace Liu: onboarding template drafts and sample repo links (due 2025-11-12)

Notes to self / scratchpad: 
- Pull previous all-hands attendance metrics and frequently-asked questions for the FAQ.
- Slack thread: #leadership-ops -> ask for verbal confirmation in this thread once execs approve.
- Consider small customer-facing note to top 5 pilot customers explaining the burst pilot and what to expect.

Appendix (links & refs):
